question: Bodyline relied on a packed leg-side field. How many fielders, besides the wicket-keeper, may now stand behind the batter's crease on that side?
answer: No more than two. Bodyline ringed the leg side with catchers while fast bowlers aimed at the batter's body, so any fend-off lobbed to a fielder. A law of 1957 allows at most two fielders, besides the wicket-keeper, behind the batter's crease on that side. Short bowling survived; the net waiting for it did not.
move: To stop a tactic, remove the piece that makes it pay.
trap: Guessing none at all, as if the whole leg-side ring were banned.
reference: Marylebone Cricket Club, The Laws of Cricket, 2017 Code, Law 28.4, 2017
